In the stark, rain-slicked streets of Gotham City, the Absolute Dark Knight operates. Stripped of the Wayne Mansion, its vast fortune, and the counsel of Alfred Pennyworth, this version of Batman is a creature of pure will and urban grit. His war is waged from the shadows of forgotten infrastructure, his arsenal built from necessity. The city’s criminal element faces a predator unburdened by legacy or resources, driven only by an uncompromising mission. Every confrontation is a raw test of endurance against the city's relentless decay.

Kelv📖 read 18 ch. ★ 5/5Short take
One of the best batman stories out there. It changes alot from the original characters in a way that makes it fit the feeling of this comic run. And it fixes my biggest issue with absolute ww in the sense that the side cast of friends are actually interesting to interact with ( to be fair his side cast are main DC characters) . But overall a very good comic
Edmundo Zárate📖 read 11 ch. ★ 5/5Short take
A really great reimagining of the bat myth. I loved how they ramped up the violence; the artwork is quite detailed—every panel really deserves to be studied closely. They took the basic elements of the story and amped them all up to the max. Comic book purists will surely find it repulsive or blasphemous, but if we make the effort to forget everything we know to avoid comparisons, it’s actually a tour de force of a read that’s a lot of fun.

Scott Snyder is unstoppable as a writer. I was already a huge fan of OG Batman but Absolute Batman made Batman new again.
